title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 81 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 471–474 (Night 81, continuing directly from nights-80), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 81 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. The second slave-girl closes her turn with sayings on abstinence and the fear of God — a poem on the two things to avoid, and a poem on provision for the afterlife — then the third speaks of the pious predecessors, of Sufyān al-Thawrī and ʿAṭāʾ al-Sulamī, and the fourth begins the stories of Bishr the Barefoot and Ibrāhīm ibn Adham, until dawn cuts Shahrazād off. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَهُ الْحَادِيَهُ وَالثَّمَانُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylahu al-ḥādiyahu wa-al-thamānūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the one-and-the-eighty,
sentences.i: And when it was the eighty-first night,
sentences.n: The print spells الليلة and الحادية with a final ه (الليله, الحاديه); the spelling is kept and read as the usual forms.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ قَلٰ لِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna al-wazīra dandāna qāla li-ḍawʾi al-makāni
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the vizier Dandān said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān:
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the vizier Dandān said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān:
sentences.n: The print runs أن into the word before it (السعيدان, “the happy — that”); it is read as two words.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ لِوَالِدِكَ الْمَرْحُومِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālati al-jāriyatu al-thāniyatu li-wālidika al-marḥūmi ʿumara bni al-nuʿmāni
sentences.l: And the slave-girl, the second, said to your father, the one-shown-mercy, ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān:
sentences.i: And the second slave-girl said to your late father, ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān:
sentences.n: The sentence is left hanging in the print; the speech that follows is the girl’s, addressed to the king’s father, as in the previous night.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ رَجُلٌ لِمُحَمَّدِ ابْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ أَوْصِنِي فَقَالَ أُوصِيكَ أَنْ تَكُونَ فِى الدُّنْيَا مَالِكًا زَاهِدًا وَفِى الْآخِرَةِ مَمْلُوكًا طَامِعًا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla rajulun li-muḥammadi ibni ʿabdi allāhi awṣinī fa-qāla ūṣīka an takūna fī al-dunyā mālikan zāhidan wa-fī al-ākhirati mamlūkan ṭāmiʿan
sentences.l: And a man said to Muḥammad son-of ʿAbd Allāh: Counsel me. So he said: I counsel you that you be in the world an owner, abstaining, and in the hereafter a owned-one, desiring.
sentences.i: A man said to Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, “Give me counsel.” He said, “I counsel you to be a master in this world, indifferent to it, and in the next a servant, eager.”
sentences.n: The print writes في as فى throughout (with the dotless ى); the same spelling recurs and is kept.

sentences.t: قَالَ وَكَيْفَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ الزَّاهِدُ فِى الدُّنْيَا يَمْلِكُ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةَ
sentences.tr: qāla wa-kayfa dhālika qāla al-zāhidu fī al-dunyā yamliku al-dunyā wa-al-ākhirata
sentences.l: He said: And how is that? He said: The abstainer in the world possesses the world and the hereafter.
sentences.i: He asked, “How so?” He said, “The man who renounces this world possesses this world and the next.”

sentences.t: وَقَالَ غَوْثُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ كَانَ آخَوَانِ فِي بَنِي اِسْرَائِيلَ قَلٰ أَحَدُهُمَا لِلْآخَرِ مَا أَخْوَفُ عَمَلٍ عَمَلَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla ghawthu bnu ʿabdi allāhi kāna ākhawāni fī banī isrāʾīla qāla aḥaduhumā li-al-ākhari mā akhwafu ʿamalin ʿamalahu
sentences.l: And Ghawth son-of ʿAbd Allāh said: There were two brothers among the sons of Israel; one of them said to the other: What is the most fearful deed that he has done?
sentences.i: Ghawth ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: There were two brothers among the Children of Israel. One said to the other, “What is the most fearful deed he has ever done?”
sentences.n: The print gives آخوان (“two brothers”) and عمله (“he did it”) where “you did” is expected; the line is slightly corrupt and is read as “the most fearful deed he has done”. The print’s قل stands for قال (pointed with the dagger alif).

sentences.t: قَلٰ لَهُ إِنِّي مَرَرْتُ بِبَيْتِ فِرَاخٍ فَأَخَذْتُ مِنْهُ وَاحِدَةً وَرَمَيْنَهَا فِي ذَلِكَ الْبَيْتِ وَلَكِنْ بَيْنَ الْفِرَاخِ الَّتِي لَمْ آخُذْهَا مِنْهَا فَهَذَا أَخْوَفُ عَمَلٍ عَمِلْنَهُ فَمَا أَخْوَفُ مَا عَمِلْتَهُ أَنْتَ
sentences.tr: qāla lahu innī marartu bi-bayti firākhin fa-akhadhtu minhu wāḥidatan wa-ramaynahā fī dhālika al-bayti wa-lākin bayna al-firākhi allatī lam ākhudhhā minhā fa-hādhā akhwafu ʿamalin ʿamilnahu fa-mā akhwafu mā ʿamiltahu anta
sentences.l: He said to him: I passed by a house of chicks, and I took from it one, and I threw it in that house, but among the chicks that I had not taken of them; so this is the most fearful deed I have done. So what is the most fearful of what you have done?
sentences.i: He said, “I once passed a nest of chicks, took one of them, and threw it back into the nest, but among the chicks I had not taken. That is the most fearful deed I have done. And you — what is the most fearful thing you have done?”
sentences.n: The print has ورمينها and عملنه, with an extra نـ (“I threw it”, “I did it”); kept as printed. The sense of ولكن بين الفراخ … is obscure: perhaps the man fears that the chick he put back was rejected by the others.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَمَّا أَنَا فَأَخْوَفُ عَمَلٍ أَعْمَلُهُ أَنِّي إِذَا قُمْتُ إِلَى الصَّلَوةِ أَخَافُ أَنْ أَكُونَ لَا أَعْمَلُ ذَلِكَ إِلَّا لِلْجَزَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ammā anā fa-akhwafu ʿamalin aʿmaluhu annī idhā qumtu ilā al-ṣalāti akhāfu an akūna lā aʿmalu dhālika illā li-al-jazāʾi
sentences.l: So he said: As for me, the most fearful deed I do is that when I stand to the prayer I fear that I am not doing that except for the reward.
sentences.i: He said, “As for me, the most fearful thing I do is this: when I stand to pray, I fear that I do it only for the reward.”
sentences.n: The print spells الصلاة as الصلوة, as in many Arabic manuscripts; the vocalisation reads it with a long ā.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ أَبُوهُمَا يَسْمَعُ كِلَاهُمَا فَقَالَ اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كَانَا صَادِقَيْنِ فَاقْبِضْهُمَا إِلَيْكَ فَقَالَ بَعْضُ الْعُقَلَاءِ إِنَّ هَذَيْنِ مِنْ أَفْضَلِ الْأَوْلَادِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna abūhumā yasmaʿu kilāhumā fa-qāla allāhumma in kānā ṣādiqayni fa-aqbiḍhumā ilayka fa-qāla baʿḍu al-ʿuqalāʾi inna hādhayni min afḍali al-awlādi
sentences.l: And their father was hearing both of them, and he said: O God, if the two are truthful, then take them to you. And one of the wise-ones said: Truly these two are among the best of children.
sentences.i: Their father was listening to both of them, and he said, “O God, if these two speak truly, take them to yourself.” And one of the wise said, “These two are among the best of sons.”
sentences.n: The print has كلاهما, “both of them”: “their father was hearing both of them”.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ عَبْدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ صَحِبْتُ فَضَالَةَ ابْنَ عُبَيْدٍ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ أَوْصِنِي فَقَالَ احْفَظْ عَنِّي هَذَيْنِ الْخَصْلَتَيْنِ أَنْ لَاتُشْرِكَ بِاللَّهِ شَيْأً وَأَنْ لَاتُؤْذِيَ مَنْ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ أَحَدًا وَأَنْشَدَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla ʿabdu bnu jubayrin ṣaḥibtu faḍālata ibna ʿubaydin fa-qultu lahu awṣinī fa-qāla iḥfaẓ ʿannī hādhayni al-khaṣlatayni an lā tushrika bi-allāhi shayʾan wa-an lā tuʾdhiya man khalaqa allāhu aḥadan wa-anshada
sentences.l: And ʿAbd son-of Jubayr said: I accompanied Faḍāla son-of ʿUbayd, and I said to him: Counsel me. So he said: Keep from me these two traits: that you not associate anything with God, and that you not harm anyone whom God has created. And he recited:
sentences.i: ʿAbd ibn Jubayr said: I kept company with Faḍāla ibn ʿUbayd and said to him, “Give me counsel.” He said, “Keep these two things from me: do not set anything beside God, and do not harm any creature God has made.” And he recited:
sentences.n: The print has شياً, “anything”, for شيئًا; the form is read as shayʾan. The speaker’s name is probably ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jubayr or ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr; the print has only عبد.

sentences.t: هَذَيْنِ الْبَيْت————يْنِ
sentences.tr: hādhayni al-bayt————ayni
sentences.l: These two verses —
sentences.i: These two verses —
sentences.n: The line of dashes is the printer’s stretched letters, a way of filling the line; the word is البيتين, “the two verses”.

sentences.t:
كُنْ كَيْفَ شِئْتَ فَاِنَّ اللّٰهَ ذُو كَرَمِ * وَانْفِ الْهُمُومَ فَمَا فِي الْاَمْرِ مِنْ بَاسِ
اِلَّا اثْنَتَيْنِ فَلَاتَقْرَبْ بِهُمَا اَبَدَا * اَشِرْكُ بِاللّٰهِ وَالْاِضْرَارُ لِلنَّاسِ
sentences.tr:
kun kayfa shiʾta fa-inna allāha dhū karami * wa-infi al-humūma fa-mā fī al-amri min bāsi
illā ithnatayni fa-lā taqrab bihumā abadan * ashrik bi-allāhi wa-al-iḍrāru li-al-nāsi
sentences.l:
Be as you wish, for God is possessor of generosity, * and drive away worries, for in the matter there is no harm,
except two; so do not approach them ever: * associating with God, and the harming of people.
sentences.i:
Be what you please, for God is generous; * put your cares away, for there is nothing amiss —
except two things: never go near them: * setting others beside God, and doing harm to men.
sentences.n: Verse copied exactly as the edition prints it, marks and all. The print has اشرك (a verb form) where the sense wants الإشراك or شِرْكٌ, “associating”; and the line’s second word بهما is printed بِهُمَا. Both are kept and read as meant.

sentences.t: وَمَا أَحْسَنَ قَوْلَ الشَّاعِرِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā aḥsana qawla al-shāʿiri
sentences.l: And how good is the saying of the poet:
sentences.i: And how fine is the poet’s verse:

sentences.t:
اِذَا اَنْتَ لَمْ يَصْحَبْكَ زَادُ مِنَ التُّقَى * وَلَاقَيْتَ بَعْدَ الْمَوْتِ مَنْ قَدْ تَزَوَّدَا
نَدِمْتَ عَلَى اَنْ لَا تَكُونَ كَمِثْلِهِ * وَاَنَّكَ لَمْ تَرْصُدْ كَمَا كَانَ اَرْصَدَا
sentences.tr:
idhā anta lam yaṣḥabka zādun mina al-tuqā * wa-lāqayta baʿda al-mawti man qad tazawwadā
nadimta ʿalā an lā takūna ka-mithlihi * wa-annaka lam tarṣud kamā kāna arṣadā
sentences.l:
If you, no provision of piety accompanies you, * and you meet after death one who has provisioned himself,
you will regret that you were not like him, * and that you did not lay up as he had laid up.
sentences.i:
If no provision of piety goes with you, * and after death you meet one who has made his provision,
you will regret not being like him, * and not having laid up as he laid up.
sentences.n: Verse copied exactly as the edition prints it, marks and all. In line 1, زاد is printed with a damma but no tanwīn (a metrical or scribal slip); the translation reads “a provision”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَقَدَّمَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ بَعْدَ أَنْ تَأَخَّرَتِ الثَّانِيَةُ وَقَالَتْ إِنَّ بَابَ الزُّهْدِ وَاسِعٌ جِدًّا وَلَكِنْ أَذْكُرُ بَعْضَ مَا يَحْضُرُنِي فِيهِ عَنِ السَّلَفِ الصَّالِحِ
sentences.tr: thumma taqaddamati al-jāriyatu al-thālithatu baʿda an taʾakhkharati al-thāniyatu wa-qālat inna bāba al-zuhdi wāsiʿun jiddan wa-lākin adhkuru baʿḍa mā yaḥḍuruni fīhi ʿani al-salafi al-ṣāliḥi
sentences.l: Then the slave-girl, the third, came forward after the second had drawn back, and she said: Truly the door of abstinence is wide, very; but I will mention some of what is present to me in it, from the predecessors, the righteous.
sentences.i: Then the third slave-girl came forward, after the second had drawn back, and said, “The door of renunciation is very wide, but I shall mention some of what comes to me of it from the righteous forebears.”

sentences.t: قَالَ بَعْضُ الْعَارِفِينَ أَنَا أَسْتَبْشِرُ بِالْمَوْتِ وَلَا أَتَيَقَّنُ فِيهِ رَاحَةً غَيْرَأَنِّي عَلِمْتُ أَنَّ الْمَوْتَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَبَيْنَ الْأَعْمَالِ فَأَرْجُو مُضَاعَفَةَ الْعَمَلِ الصَّالِحِ وَانْقِطَاعَ الْعَمَلِ السَّيِّءِ
sentences.tr: qāla baʿḍu al-ʿārifīna anā astabshiru bi-al-mawti wa-lā atayaqqanu fīhi rāḥatan ghayra annī ʿalimtu anna al-mawta yaḥūlu bayna al-marʾi wa-bayna al-aʿmāli fa-arjū muḍāʿafata al-ʿamali al-ṣāliḥi wa-inqiṭāʿa al-ʿamali al-sayyiʾi
sentences.l: One of the knowers said: I rejoice at death, and I am not certain of rest in it, except that I know that death comes between a man and deeds; so I hope for the doubling of good deeds and the cutting-off of bad deeds.
sentences.i: One of the gnostics said, “I rejoice at death, though I am not sure of finding rest in it; but I know that death comes between a man and his works, so I hope for the multiplying of good works and the ceasing of evil ones.”
sentences.n: The print has غيراني for غير أني (run together); read as two words. العارفين, “the knowers”, are the Sufi gnostics.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ عَطَاءٌ السَّلَمِيُّ إِذَا فَرَغَ مِنْ وَصِيَّتِهِ انْتَفَضَ وَارْتَعَدَ وَبَكَى بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا فَقِيلَ لَهُ لِمَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna ʿaṭāʾun al-salamiyyu idhā faragha min waṣiyyatihi intafaḍa wa-irtaʿada wa-bakā bukāʾan shadīdan fa-qīla lahu lima dhālika
sentences.l: And ʿAṭāʾ al-Sulamī, when he finished his testament, would shake and tremble and weep a hard weeping; so it was said to him: Why that?
sentences.i: When ʿAṭāʾ al-Sulamī had finished making his will, he would shake and tremble and weep bitterly; and he was asked, “Why is that?”
sentences.n: The print has عطاء السلمي with no link between name and nisba; the nisba is read al-Salamī or al-Sulamī, a name found in the early Sufi record. The word وصيته, “his testament”, is used here for the prayer-will he recited before standing to pray.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ إِنِّي أُرِيدَانِ أَقْبَلَ عَلَى أَمْرٍ عَظِيمٍ وَهُوَ الِانْتِصَابُ بَيْنَ يَدَىِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى لِلْعَمَلِ بِمُقْتَضَى الْوَصِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla innī urīdāni aqbala ʿalā amrin ʿaẓīmin wa-huwa al-intiṣābu bayna yadayi allāhi taʿālā li-al-ʿamali bi-muqtaḍā al-waṣiyyati
sentences.l: So he said: Truly I am about to turn to a great matter, and it is the standing between the hands of God, exalted, for the doing according to the requirement of the testament.
sentences.i: He said, “I am about to approach a great matter: standing before God Most High to act on the terms of the will.”
sentences.n: The print has اريدان اقبل, with the ان run into the verb; read as أريد أن أُقبل. For يدى the print’s ى is dotless; read as يَدَيْ in the construct.

sentences.t: وَلِذَلِكَ كَانَ عَلِيٌّ زَيْنُ الْعَابِدِينَ ابْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ يَرْتَعِدُ إِذَا قَامَ لِلصَّلَوةِ فَسُئِلَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ أَتَدْرُونَ لِمَنْ أَقُومُ وَلِمَنْ أُخَاطِبُ
sentences.tr: wa-li-dhālika kāna ʿaliyyun zaynu al-ʿābidīna ibnu al-ḥusayni yartaʿidu idhā qāma li-al-ṣalāti fa-suʾila ʿan dhālika fa-qāla atadrūna li-man aqūmu wa-li-man ukhāṭibu
sentences.l: And for that reason ʿAlī Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn son-of al-Ḥusayn used to tremble when he stood to the prayer; and he was asked about that, and he said: Do you know for whom I stand, and to whom I speak?
sentences.i: This is why ʿAlī Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn ibn al-Ḥusayn would tremble when he stood to pray; asked about it, he said, “Do you know before whom I stand and to whom I speak?”
sentences.n: The print has عليّ with a shadda, kept in the vocalisation.

sentences.t: وَقِيلَ كَانَ بِجَانِبِ سُفْيَانَ الثَّوْرِيِّ رَجُلٌ ضَرِيرٌ فَإِذَا كَانَ شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ يَخْرُجُ وَيُصَلِّى بِالنَّاسِ فَيَسْكُتُ وَيُبْطِيءُ
sentences.tr: wa-qīla kāna bi-jānibi sufyāna al-thawriyyi rajulun ḍarīrun fa-idhā kāna shahru ramaḍāna yakhruju wa-yuṣallī bi-al-nāsi fa-yaskutu wa-yubṭīʾu
sentences.l: And it was said: There was beside Sufyān al-Thawrī a man, blind; and when it was the month of Ramaḍān he would go out and lead the people in prayer, and he would fall silent and be slow.
sentences.i: It is said that beside Sufyān al-Thawrī there was a blind man, who in the month of Ramaḍān would go out and lead the people in prayer, and then fall silent and hesitate.
sentences.n: The meaning of فيسكت ويبطيء, “he would be silent and be slow”, is obscure; perhaps he paused in his recitation from awe.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ سُفْيَانُ إِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ أُتِيَ بِأَهْلِ الْقُرْآنِ فَيُمَيَّزُونَ بِعَلَامَةِ مَزِيدِ الْكَرَامَةِ عَمَّنْ سِوَاهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla sufyānu idhā kāna yawmu al-qiyāmati utiya bi-ahli al-qurʾāni fa-yumayyazūna bi-ʿalāmati mazīdi al-karāmati ʿamman siwāhum
sentences.l: And Sufyān said: When it is the Day of Resurrection, the people of the Qurʾān are brought, and they are distinguished by a sign of increase of honour from those besides them.
sentences.i: Sufyān said: On the Day of Resurrection the people of the Qurʾān will be brought forth, and set apart from all others by a sign of greater honour.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ سُفْيَانُ لَوْ أَنَّ النَّفْسَ اسْتَقَرَّتْ فِى الْقَلْبِ كَمَا يَنْبَغِي لَطَارَ فَرَحًا وَشَوْقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ وَحُزْنًا وَخَوْفًا مِنَ النَّارِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla sufyānu law anna al-nafsa istaqarrat fī al-qalbi kamā yanbaghī la-ṭāra faraḥan wa-shawqan ilā al-jannati wa-ḥuznan wa-khawfan mina al-nāri
sentences.l: And Sufyān said: If the soul were settled in the heart as is fitting, it would fly, in joy and longing for the Garden, and in grief and fear of the Fire.
sentences.i: Sufyān said: If the soul were settled in the heart as it should be, it would fly with joy and longing for Paradise, and with grief and fear of the Fire.

sentences.t: وَعَنْ سُفْيَانَ الثَّوْرِيِّ أَنَّهُ قَالَ النَّظَرُ إِلَى وَجْهِ الظَّالِمِ خَطِيئَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿan sufyāna al-thawriyyi annahu qāla al-naẓaru ilā wajhi al-ẓālimi khaṭīʾatun
sentences.l: And from Sufyān al-Thawrī, that he said: The looking at the face of the wrongdoer is a sin.
sentences.i: And it is told of Sufyān al-Thawrī that he said, “To look upon the face of a tyrant is a sin.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَأَخَّرَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ وَتَقَدَّمَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ الرَّابِعَةُ وَقَالَتْ وَهَا أَنَا أَتَكَلَّمُ بِبَعْضِ مَا يَحْضُرُنِي مِنْ أَخْبَارِ الصَّالِحِينَ
sentences.tr: thumma taʾakhkharati al-jāriyatu al-thālithatu wa-taqaddamati al-jāriyatu al-rābiʿatu wa-qālat wa-hā anā atakallamu bi-baʿḍi mā yaḥḍuruni min akhbāri al-ṣāliḥīna
sentences.l: Then the slave-girl, the third, drew back and the slave-girl, the fourth, came forward and said: And here am I, speaking some of what is present to me of the reports of the righteous.
sentences.i: Then the third slave-girl drew back and the fourth came forward and said, “Here I speak of such tales of the righteous as come to me.”

sentences.t: رُوِيَ أَنَّ بِشْرًا الْحَافِي قَالَ سَمِعْتُ خَالِدًا يَقُولُ إِيَّاكُمْ وَسَرَائِرَ الشِّرْكِ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ وَمَا سَرَائِرُ الشِّرْكِ قَالَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَيُطِيلَ رُكُوعَهُ وَسُجُودَهُ حَتَّى يَلْحَقَهُ الْحَدَثُ
sentences.tr: ruwiya anna bishran al-ḥāfiya qāla samiʿtu khālidan yaqūlu iyyākum wa-sarāʾira al-shirki fa-qultu lahu wa-mā sarāʾiru al-shirki qāla an yuṣalliya aḥadukum fa-yuṭīla rukūʿahu wa-sujūdahu ḥattā yalḥaqahu al-ḥadathu
sentences.l: It is related that Bishr the Barefoot said: I heard Khālid saying: Beware of the secrets of association. So I said to him: And what are the secrets of association? He said: That one of you pray, and lengthen his bowing and his prostration, until the impurity reaches him.
sentences.i: It is related that Bishr the Barefoot said, “I heard Khālid say: Beware the hidden forms of idolatry.” I asked him, “What are the hidden forms of idolatry?” He said, “That one of you should pray and prolong his bowing and prostration until he is taken by the need to relieve himself.”
sentences.n: The print has ايّاكم with a shadda. الحدث is ritual impurity; the sense is that the man prolongs his prayer for show, so long that he is overtaken by it. Hidden shirk (سرائر الشرك) here is showing off in worship.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ بَعْضُ الْعَارِفِينَ فِعْلُ الْحَسَنَاتِ يُكَفِّرُ السَّيِّئَاتِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla baʿḍu al-ʿārifīna fiʿlu al-ḥasanāti yukaffiru al-sayyiʾāti
sentences.l: And one of the knowers said: The doing of good deeds expiates bad deeds.
sentences.i: One of the gnostics said, “The doing of good deeds wipes out evil deeds.”

sentences.t: وَقَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ الْتَمَسْتُ مِنْ بِشْرِ بْنِ الْحَافِي شَيْأً مِنْ أَسْرَارِ الْحَقَائِقِ فَقَالَ يَابُنَيَّ هَذَا الْعِلْمُ لَايَنْبَغِي أَنْ نُعَلِّمَهُ كُلَّ أَحَدٍ فَمِنْ كُلِّ مِائَةٍ خَمْسَةٌ مِثْلُ زَكَوةِ الدِّرْهَمِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla ibrāhīmu iltamastu min bishri bni al-ḥāfī shayʾan min asrāri al-ḥaqāʾiqi fa-qāla yā-bunayya hādhā al-ʿilmu lā yanbaghī an nuʿallimahu kulla aḥadin fa-min kulli miʾatin khamsatun mithlu zakāti al-dirhami
sentences.l: And Ibrāhīm said: I asked of Bishr son-of the Barefoot something of the secrets of the realities; so he said: O my little son, this knowledge, it is not fitting that we teach it to everyone; of every hundred, five — like the almsgiving of the dirham.
sentences.i: Ibrāhīm said: I asked Bishr the Barefoot for something of the secrets of the true realities. He said, “My son, this knowledge should not be taught to everyone; of every hundred, five — as with the alms-due on a dirham.”
sentences.n: The print has يابنّي and زكوة (for زكاة), kept. Zakāt on silver is one fortieth, 2.5 in a hundred; the saying says the secrets belong to five in a hundred. The print’s بشر بن الحافي, “Bishr son of the Barefoot”, is a slip for بشر الحافي.

sentences.t: قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ أَدْهَمَ فَاسْتَحْلَيْتُ كَلَامَهُ وَاسْتَحْسَنْتُهُ فَبَيْنَمَا أَنَا أُصَلِّي وَإِذَا بِبِشْرٍ يُصَلِّي فَقُمْتُ وَرَاءَهُ أَرْكَعُ إِلَى أَنْ يُؤَذِّنَ الْمُؤَذِّنُ
sentences.tr: qāla ibrāhīmu bnu adhama fa-staḥlaytu kalāmahu wa-staḥsantuhu fa-baynamā anā uṣallī wa-idhā bi-bishrin yuṣallī fa-qumtu warāʾahu arkaʿu ilā an yuʾadhdhina al-muʾadhdhinu
sentences.l: Ibrāhīm son-of Adham said: So I found his speech sweet and thought it good; and while I was praying, then behold, Bishr was praying; so I stood behind him bowing, until the muezzin should call.
sentences.i: Ibrāhīm ibn Adham said: I found his words sweet and fine; and as I was praying, there was Bishr praying too, so I stood behind him, bowing, until the muezzin gave the call.
sentences.n: The print here has اصلّي with a shadda. For وإذا ببشر, the بـ follows إذا of surprise and only marks what appears: “and behold, Bishr”.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ رَجُلٌ رَثُّ الْحَالَةِ وَقَالَ يَا قَوْمُ احْذَرُوا الصِّدْقَ الضَّارَّ وَلَا بَأْسَ بِالْكَذِبِ النَّافِعِ وَلَيْسَ مَعَ الِاضْطِرَارِ اخْتِيَارٌ وَلَايَنْفَعُ الْكَلَامُ عِنْدَ الْعَدَمِ كَمَا لَايَضُرُّ السُّكُوتُ عِنْدَ وُجُودِ الْجُودِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma rajulun rathchu al-ḥālati wa-qāla yā qawmi iḥdharū al-ṣidqa al-ḍārra wa-lā baʾsa bi-al-kadhibi al-nāfiʿi wa-laysa maʿa al-iḍṭirāri ikhtiyārun wa-lā yanfaʿu al-kalāmu ʿinda al-ʿadami kamā lā yaḍurru al-sukūtu ʿinda wujūdi al-jūdi
sentences.l: So a man stood, shabby of state, and said: O people, beware the harmful truth; and there is no harm in the useful lie; and with compulsion there is no choice; and speech does not benefit at non-existence, as silence does not harm at the existence of generosity.
sentences.i: A man in tattered state stood up and said, “People, beware a truth that does harm; there is no sin in a lie that does good. Where there is compulsion there is no choice, and speech is no use in want, as silence does no harm where there is bounty.”
sentences.n: A saying whose point is obscure; the translation follows the words. الجود, “generosity”, and العدم, “want / non-existence”, are paired as opposites.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ رَأَيْتُ بِشْرًا سَقَطَ مِنْهُ دَانِقٌ فَقُمْتُ إِلَيْهِ وَأَعْطَيْتُهُ دِرْهَمًا فَقَالَ لَا آخُذُهُ فَقُلْتُ إِنَّهُ مِنْ خَالِصِ الْحَلَالِ فَقَالَ لِي أَنَا لَسْتُ أَسْتَبْدِلُ نِعَمَ الدُّنْيَا بِنِعَمِ الْآخِرَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla ibrāhīmu raʾaytu bishran saqaṭa minhu dāniqun fa-qumtu ilayhi wa-aʿṭaytuhu dirhaman fa-qāla lā ākhudhuhu fa-qultu innahu min khāliṣi al-ḥalāli fa-qāla lī anā lastu astabdilu niʿama al-dunyā bi-niʿami al-ākhirati
sentences.l: And Ibrāhīm said: I saw Bishr; a danaq fell from him, so I got up to him and gave him a dirham, and he said: I do not take it. So I said: It is of the purest lawful. So he said to me: I am not one to exchange the blessings of the world for the blessings of the hereafter.
sentences.i: Ibrāhīm said: I saw Bishr drop a danaq, and I went to him and gave him a dirham. He said, “I will not take it.” I said, “It is wholly lawful gain.” He said, “I will not trade the blessings of this world for the blessings of the next.”
sentences.n: A dāniq is a sixth of a dirham, a very small coin.

sentences.t: وَيُرْوَى أَنَّ أُخْتَ بِشْرٍ الْحَافِي قَصَدَتْ أَحْمَدَ بْنَ حَنْبَلٍ
sentences.tr: wa-yurwā anna ukhta bishrin al-ḥāfī qaṣadat aḥmada bna ḥanbalin
sentences.l: And it is related that the sister of Bishr the Barefoot made for Aḥmad son-of Ḥanbal,
sentences.i: It is also told that the sister of Bishr the Barefoot went to Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal,
sentences.n: The sentence breaks off here at dawn; it continues in the next night.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَنَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahra zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakanat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she became still from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Then morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell quiet, leaving the permitted tale unsaid.
sentences.n: The print has فسكنت (“she became still”), where the earlier nights have فسكتت.
